blockNote: Boot-logo palette thinker (Bank 00, 47207-47226): the third of the three thinkers that scene $FB's thinker list (thinker_spawn_0CEB1D, slot 2, param #03, never read) spawns together with boot_logo_palette_enix and boot_logo_palette_quintet. All three run side by side in BOTH visits of the scene (sFB_boot_logo reloads the scene for the second logo).

It plays palette bundles $56, $57 and $58 in order (PaletteStart selects a bundle, PaletteStep runs it to its end), then KillThinker. The bundles write CGRAM colors $A1 to $AF, colors 1 to 15 of OBJ palette 2 (30 bytes per frame, 8 frames per bundle, 1 extra tick per frame, 33 on the last frame of $58).
$56: starts black and fills the 15 colors with the flat purple $68DA one at a time (colors 1 to 8 over the 8 frames).
$57: continues the fill from 9 colors to all 15 (the last two frames are both full).

$58: starts all purple; a darker dip opens around color 7 and gets wider and deeper each frame, ending in a V-shaped ramp from $64B9 at the ends down to $3C4F in the middle (colors 14 and 15 stay $68DA / $70DC), which is held for 34 ticks.
This is read from the colour values (not run).
=== WHERE THE COLOURS LAND ===

OBJ palette 2 is used only by the 4 x 2 block of 16 x 16 parts under the emblem in sprite_group_000010 (parts $10 to $17 of the second logo, see spm_boot_logos). The first logo is on OBJ palette 3, which no thinker touches, so in the first visit this thinker runs unseen.
=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header called this the 'third and final logo palette thinker' that 'completes the boot logo palette rotation before gameplay begins' and described #56, #57 and #58 as palette animations. It is the third of three parallel thinkers, not a later step, #56 to #58 are palette bundles, and it animates only OBJ palette 2 of the second logo.

blockNote: Boot-logo palette thinker (Bank 00, 47167-47186). Scene $FB's thinker list (thinker_spawn_0CEB1D, slot 0, param #01) spawns it together with boot_logo_palette_quintet and boot_logo_palette_third. All three start with the scene and run side by side, in BOTH visits of scene $FB (sFB_boot_logo reloads the scene for the second logo), so each visit animates OBJ palettes 0, 1 and 2 at once. Only the second logo (sprite_group_000010 in spm_boot_logos) uses those palettes, so only it changes colour; the first logo is on OBJ palette 3, which no thinker touches, so in the first visit these thinkers run unseen.

This thinker plays palette bundles $50, $52 and $54 in order: PaletteStart selects a bundle and PaletteStep runs it to its end (the op continues only when the bundle is finished), three times, then KillThinker. The param byte #01 is never read (PaletteStart overwrites animScratch+2 with the bundle ID). Header word $0800: bit 11 keeps it running in the lighter frame routines, bit 2 is clear (runs before the actors).
=== THE BUNDLES (palette_bundles, bank $16) ===

Each bundle has 8 sub-entries of one frame each. A frame is 15 colors (30 bytes) written to CGRAM colors $81 to $8F, i.e. colors 1 to 15 of OBJ palette 0 (the Quintet thinker writes $91 to $9F, OBJ palette 1, and the third thinker $A1 to $AF, OBJ palette 2). There is 1 extra tick between frames in $50 and $52 and 3 in $54.

$50: starts all black; a 13-color ramp from dark purple ($2C4B) to white ($7FFF) grows across colors 1 to 13, its white tip moving from color 1 to color 13 with the darker colors trailing it; colors 14 and 15 stay 0.
$52: the ramp turns white from its bright end towards its dark end until all 13 colors are white, while colors 14 and 15 brighten from $18C6 / $2108 to $4E73 / $6739.
$54: starts all white and fades back down to the ramp (steps through $777D, $6AFA, ... to $2C4B ... $7FFF) while colors 14 and 15 darken to $1425 / $2449.
So the logo's palette sweeps in, flashes to white and settles on a rainbow ramp: a shine effect. This is read from the colour values (not run).
=== WHERE THE COLOURS LAND ===

In sprite_group_000010 (the second logo, spm_boot_logos) OBJ palette 0 colours 8 of the 16 parts of the 4 x 4 emblem block (parts $05 to $0A, $0E, $0F: the lower two rows), OBJ palette 1 the other 8 (parts $00 to $04, $0B to $0D: the upper two rows). Both get the same shine at the same time, so the emblem sweeps in, flashes white and settles.
=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header said it is the first of three thinkers and 'animates the Enix logo colors'; the Quintet note said it runs 'after the Enix palette sequence'. They are spawned together and run in parallel. The names come from the spawn order only: the thinker belongs to the second logo's emblem, and which company's logo that is was not checked against the tile art (OQ-I055-1). I054 left the question of which logo uses OBJ palettes 0 and 1 open (OQ-I054-1); the sprite tables answer it.

Boot-logo palette thinker (Bank 00, 47187-47206): the twin of boot_logo_palette_enix. Spawned together with it and boot_logo_palette_third by scene $FB's thinker list (thinker_spawn_0CEB1D, slot 1, param #02, never read) and run in parallel with them in both visits of the scene.

Plays palette bundles $51, $53 and $55 in order (PaletteStart + PaletteStep each), then KillThinker. The bundles hold exactly the same colour frames as $50, $52 and $54 (see boot_logo_palette_enix) but write them to CGRAM colors $91 to $9F, colors 1 to 15 of OBJ palette 1, with the same 1 / 1 / 3 extra ticks. So the effect is a black to rainbow-ramp reveal, a white flash and a settle.

OBJ palette 1 colours 8 of the 16 parts of the 4 x 4 emblem block of the second logo (parts $00 to $04 and $0B to $0D of sprite_group_000010: the upper two rows); the Enix thinker does the other 8 with palette 0. The first logo does not use it.
=== CORRECTIONS ===

The old header said it runs 'after the Enix palette sequence'; it runs at the same time. The I054 note gave the spawn param as #01; the three slots carry #01, #02 and #03 and this one is #02 (none is read). Which logo uses OBJ palette 1 (OQ-I054-1) is answered by the sprite tables: the second logo's emblem. Which company's logo that is was not checked (OQ-I055-1).

Boot logo sequence actor - scene $FB master controller (the first scene of the game). Scene $FB is entered TWICE at power-on and shows one logo per visit; the second logo then hands over to the title screen scene $FC.
=== SEQUENCE ===

1. BootLogoInit (both visits): sets displayModeFlags bit 14 (no reader found, OQ-I034-1), clears colour 0 of the palette staging buffer, enables FastROM (MEMSEL = $01), puts only the sprite layer on the main screen (TM = $10, bit 4 = OBJ; no BG is shown), masks the joypad, then reads STAT78 bit 4: 0 = 60 Hz NTSC continues, 1 = 50 Hz PAL jumps to BootLogoPalTextFallback.

2. First visit (event flag $10 clear): nudge the actor Y -16, play sprite animation #01 (sprite_group_000112, a 96 x 48 logo on OBJ palette 3) for 2 passes of 60 ticks = 120 ticks, set event flag $10, QueueMapChange to scene $FB itself, Die.

3. Second visit (flag set): BootLogoSecondPhase plays animation #00 (sprite_group_000010, an emblem with a wordmark under it, OBJ palettes 0, 1, 2 and 4) for 120 ticks, clears flag $10 and queues scene $FC (title screen), Die.

Event flag $10 is not one of the flags the scene load zeroes (only $00 to $0F are), which is why it survives the reload; it is cleared again at the end because the South Cape church scripts (sc08_*) use the same flag.
The three boot_logo_palette_* thinkers are spawned by the scene's thinker list in both visits and animate OBJ palettes 0, 1 and 2, i.e. only the second logo (see boot_logo_palette_enix).
=== PAL LOCKOUT ===

A 50 Hz console never sees a logo: BootLogoPalTextFallback draws the region warning text (consolestring_01D9D8) on BG3 and then yields forever at SetEntryHere + RTL. The game cannot be started on a PAL console.
=== POSITION ===

The scene's actor-spawn places the actor at tile (7, 8) and InitActorFromSceneData adds 8 pixels of X for normal actors; the first NudgePosition adds another 8, so the actor ends at X = 128, the centre of the 256-pixel screen. The sprite groups are laid out around that origin. QueueMapChange's last operand $1100 is the packed camera-bounds override (InitCameraBounds).
=== SPRITES (spm_boot_logos.sprite.asm) ===

The scene's spritemap card loads spm_boot_logos ($018F bytes) to $7E4000; its two entries are the animation indexes of StageSpriteLoop: #00 = sprite_set_000004 (second logo), #01 = sprite_set_00000A (first logo). Each sprite-set is one frame record (hold $003B = 60 ticks per pass, group pointer) closed by the hidden $FFFF delimiter.
First logo, sprite_group_000112: 96 x 48 px, 16 parts of 16 x 16 in rows of 6, 6 and 4, all OBJ palette 3.

Second logo, sprite_group_000010: 122 x 156 px, 35 parts: a 4 x 4 block (64 x 64) on OBJ palette 1 (upper two rows) and 0 (lower two rows), a 4 x 2 block below it on palette 2, and a row of 11 parts 12 px apart on palette 4. Palettes 0 to 2 are the ones the boot_logo_palette_* thinkers animate; palette 4 is static.

Sprite-part = 7 bytes: size flag, X offset and mirrored X, Y offset and mirrored Y, OAM tile word (high byte vhppPPPN, PPP = OBJ palette). Sprite-group = 12 header bytes (X extents left / right, Y extents above / below, 8 bytes nothing reads, identical in both groups), the part count, then the parts. The palettes come from pal_boot_logos (80 colours, OBJ palettes 0 to 4, loaded at CGRAM colour 128). Which company's logo each group draws was not checked against the tile art (OQ-I055-1).
=== NOTES ===

The joypad mask in the ROM is $FFFC (db-us/transforms.json rewrites $FFF0 to $FFFC for this block), which hides every pad bit including Start and Select, so no logo can be skipped. The old header said TM = $10 puts BG1 on the main screen and that the mask is $FFF0; TM bit 4 is the OBJ layer and the shipped mask is $FFFC.

partNotes.BootLogoInit: Entry, both visits. Display set-up (bit 14 of displayModeFlags, black backdrop, FastROM, TM = OBJ only, joypad mask), then STAT78 bit 4 decides: 60 Hz falls through to loc_0BC8EA, 50 Hz jumps to BootLogoPalTextFallback.
partNotes.loc_0BC8EA: NTSC path. Centres the actor (X +8), then splits on event flag $10: set = second visit (BootLogoSecondPhase); clear = first visit: Y -16, animation #01 for 2 passes, set the flag, reload scene $FB, Die.
partNotes.BootLogoSecondPhase: Second visit: animation #00 (the emblem logo) for 2 passes of 60 ticks, clear event flag $10, QueueMapChange to scene $FC (title screen) with the same $1100 camera-bounds operand, Die.
partNotes.BootLogoPalTextFallback: PAL lockout screen. Copies the first 8 colours of pal_ending_comet into staging colours 0 to 7, forces colour 0 to black, draws the region warning (consolestring_01D9D8) on BG3 and sets TM = $04 (BG3 only). The actor then yields every frame at the SetEntryHere / RTL pair and never leaves. Only the warning is drawn: PUSH START and the copyright string belong to the title scene.
